newsitem.title: UK: Loving rat mums have stress-free babies - report.
newsitem.headline: Loving rat mums have stress-free babies - report.

text.p: Rats with loving and attentive mothers are much more adventurous and can handle stress better, Canadian researchers said on Thursday.
Dong Lui and a team at McGill University's Douglas Hospital Centre in Verdun, Quebec studied nine rats rearing their litters and found that the level of care varied widely.
The offspring of mothers who nursed, groomed and licked them more were then confined in narrow plastic tubes for 20 minutes, the researchers told The New Scientist weekly.
The researchers found that the stress hormone levels of the lovingly nurtured rats were much lower. They also calmed down much more quickly and began exploring again, they said.
